title: ERC-8262 provider protocol vector set
description: Shape of vectors.json. The embedded `discovery` and `evidence` documents are validated by provider-discovery.schema.json and provider-evidence.schema.json, not here.

clockSkewSeconds.description: Tolerated disagreement between clocks (SPEC.md section 10.5, Clocks).

maxListItems.description: Most entries in each discovery list: deployments, keys, sources, and claims per source.

minRevocationCheckSeconds.description: Smallest revocationCheckSeconds a discovery document may declare, and smallest deployment maximum a consumer may set (SPEC.md section 10.7, Held grants).

maxRevocationCheckSeconds.description: Largest revocationCheckSeconds a discovery document may declare, and largest deployment maximum a consumer may set (SPEC.md section 10.7, Held grants).

maxTimestamp.description: Largest timestamp either document may carry (2^32 - 1 Unix seconds).

minUngrantedRevocationsPerAnnouncer.description: Least bound a consumer may set on the evidence revocations (a 410 or a revoked body) it records for ids no grant rests on, per (trust domain, announcing party as the consumer authenticated it), never per subject wallet, and on one trust domain's unattributed announcements; the trust domain's own callback or push is not charged to it only when the consumer authenticates it as the provider's (a credential set up with the provider, never a source address or host header). No other record counts, revocations of granted ids are never bounded or dropped, and over the bound such a revocation is refused but not recorded: every announcement is still evaluated (SPEC.md section 10.7, Revocation bound).

maxBlockAgeSeconds.description: Oldest the latest block of a block pair may be by the consumer's clock: an older one is stale, so an evaluation that can grant on it is unavailable (blocks_stale): it grants nothing and suspends a held grant (SPEC.md section 10.5, Block pair).

follows.description: An earlier evaluation case. This case's observation store (context.seenDiscovery, seenEvidence, seenRevoked and heldGrants) is exactly the earlier case's store plus what it wrote (expected.records) and the grant it touched (the entry for its subject, discovery host and announced evidenceId) as it left it (kept: recheckBy set to expected.recheckBy; suspended: recheckBy null; replaced: resting on the earlier case's proof, its proofHash, attestation expiresAt and recheckBy; untouched: unchanged; ended: removed; a grant the earlier store did not hold is not created; every other grant untouched): a consumer runs the chain on its own store.

evidence.description: The evidence fixture (or schema case); when context.evidenceFetch.status is not 200 it is the document the announced id names, and no document is evaluated.

trustDomainId.description: The independently controlled signing domain: the lowercase DNS host that serves this provider's discovery document and evidence endpoint. A document is authoritative only when fetched over https, without redirects, from this exact host: the consumer compares the serialized host of the URL it fetched with this value as exact ASCII. Never an IP literal: the last label starts with a letter, so no WHATWG URL parser reads the host as an IPv4 address. The host proves nothing about the attestor: the consumer's allowlist pins each trust domain to its attestorProviderId per Oracle deployment, and a host it does not list is refused.

attestorProviderId.description: The ERC-8262 Oracle `providerId` (uint256: nonzero and at most 2^256 - 1) that attests for this trust domain on the paired deployment, as a canonical decimal string. Self-asserted: a consumer accepts it only when it equals the attestor its allowlist pins for the trust domain.

The ERC-8262 Oracle `providerId` (uint256: nonzero and at most 2^256 - 1) that attests for this trust domain on the paired deployment, as a canonical decimal string. Self-asserted: a consumer accepts it only when it equals the attestor its allowlist pins for the trust domain.

credentialRoots.description: Roots the Oracle holds valid (isValidCredentialRoot) and registered to the attestor (getCredentialRoot(root).providerId).

validConfigs.description: Config hashes the Oracle holds valid: isValidConfig(configHash), read at step 23 for the configHash of a statement for the evidence's proof type (7, 8 or 9).

seenDiscovery.description: Discovery fixtures in the consumer's observation store, each with the attestorProviderId its key revocations were recorded under: the attestor the consumer pinned its trust domain to on this deployment when it recorded it, if the document's own entry for this deployment named that attestor; null otherwise (they then apply to that trust domain alone, SPEC.md section 10.7, Revocation).

oneOf.description: The ERC-8262 Oracle `providerId` (uint256: nonzero and at most 2^256 - 1) that attests for this trust domain on the paired deployment, as a canonical decimal string. Self-asserted: a consumer accepts it only when it equals the attestor its allowlist pins for the trust domain.

seenEvidence.description: Active evidence fixtures in the consumer's observation store.

seenRevoked.description: (trustDomainId, evidenceId) pairs the consumer recorded as revoked from a 410 or a revoked body, trustDomainId being the allowlisted host it came from.

Never an IP literal: the last label starts with a letter, so no WHATWG URL parser reads the host as an IPv4 address. The host proves nothing about the attestor: the consumer's allowlist pins each trust domain to its attestorProviderId per Oracle deployment, and a host it does not list is refused.

evidenceId.description: Replay: an unguessable capability (at least 128 bits, base64url), unique for the provider's lifetime and never reused. A consumer validates an announced id against this rule before using it, requests exactly `https://{trustDomainId}/v1/erc8262/evidence/` followed by the id, and refuses a body whose evidenceId differs (exact comparison). It keys what it has observed by (trustDomainId, evidenceId). Re-delivery with identical immutable fields is idempotent and counts once; any differing immutable field is refused. Renewal is a new evidenceId.

statement.description: The statement the consumer requires the proof to prove (SPEC.md section 10.5, step 30), tagged with the proof type it is for: null for proof type 4 (the evidence's credentialType is the statement); for 7 the accepted jurisdiction ids and the config_hash; for 8 the risk proof_type and config_hash with, for a threshold (1), its direction (1 GT, 2 LT) and bound_lower, or for a range (2), bound_lower and bound_upper (risk_score_signed leaves the other word free in each mode); for 9 those of 7 plus the least threshold_m.

jurisdictionIds.description: The ERC-8262 jurisdiction ids the consumer accepts.
The ERC-8262 jurisdiction ids the consumer accepts.

latest.description: The revocation and denial reads at the latest block (SPEC.md section 10.5, Oracle reads), where they differ from the finalized reads the rest of the context gives; null when they are the same. registry: isProviderDenied (step 21) and the roots and signer hashes registered to each attestor (step 23); its credentialSigner is never read, since step 22 reads only at the finalized block. validConfigs: isValidConfig (step 23). attestationRevoked: isAttestationRevoked of the proof (step 31). A refusal at either block refuses; a step-31 revocation seen only here suspends a held grant rather than ending it.

attestorProviderId.description: The ERC-8262 Oracle `providerId` (uint256: nonzero and at most 2^256 - 1) that attests for this trust domain on the paired deployment, as a canonical decimal string. Self-asserted: a consumer accepts it only when it equals the attestor its allowlist pins for the trust domain.

credentialRoots.description: Roots the Oracle holds valid (isValidCredentialRoot) and registered to the attestor (getCredentialRoot(root).providerId).

blocks.description: The block pair the evaluation (or the quorum) resolved, checked against the consumer's clock (context.now) before its first Oracle read (SPEC.md section 10.5, Block pair; a quorum checks it once every member's fetches have completed, section 10.6): the node's eth_chainId and the finalized and latest blocks' number and timestamp. Invalid when chainId is not the deployment's, the finalized block is after the latest one (number or timestamp; equal is not after), or the latest block's timestamp is more than clockSkewSeconds after the consumer's clock; else stale when the latest block's timestamp is more than maxBlockAgeSeconds before the consumer's clock.

heldGrants.description: The grants the consumer's observation store holds (SPEC.md section 10.7, Held grants), at most one per key: the subject it was granted to, the discovery host (trustDomainId) and the announced evidenceId it was granted on. Each record carries the proofHash of the proof it rests on, the attestation expiresAt read when that proof was accepted (the grant ends then at the latest, whatever any evaluation decides) and recheckBy. The entry for this case's subject, discovery host and announced evidenceId, if any, is the grant expected.heldGrant describes: re-evaluated when it rests on context.proof.proofHash (what happens to it does not depend on its state), else evaluated against another proof, which can replace or end it but never suspends it. Every other entry is another grant (another subject's, host's or id's), which this evaluation never touches.

recheckBy.description: When the grant's next re-evaluation is due (SPEC.md section 10.7, Held grants): the consumer's clock at its last accepting evaluation plus the smaller of the revocationCheckSeconds of the discovery document that evaluation read and the consumer's maxRecheckSeconds (a consumer that lowers its maximum clamps it). The grant is exercised only before it. null while the grant is suspended.

maxRecheckSeconds.description: The consumer's deployment maximum on a grant's re-evaluation interval (SPEC.md section 10.7, Held grants): a grant's next re-evaluation is due at most this many seconds after its last accepting one, whatever revocationCheckSeconds the provider declares, and a failed or suspending re-evaluation is retried within it on the grant's own schedule, whatever the host's fetch backoff. At least 60 (limits.minRevocationCheckSeconds) and at most limits.maxRevocationCheckSeconds.

status.description: The HTTP status; null when no HTTP response arrived (a timeout, a TLS or connection failure).
The HTTP status; null when no HTTP response arrived (a timeout, a TLS or connection failure).

announcedEvidenceId.description: The evidenceId the consumer was given (announcement or its own record). Not necessarily valid: the consumer checks it against the evidence schema's evidenceId rule before building the URL.

proof.description: The Oracle-verified proof the evidence feeds, as the consumer reads it (SPEC.md section 10.5, steps 30-31). proofHash: the hash the Oracle indexes the proof by, which keys a grant made on it (section 10.7, Held grants). publicInputs: the publicInputs bytes of the submitCompliance call that verified it, as 32-byte lowercase hex words in ERC-8262 order (the section 10.5 layout table); the consumer accepts them only if keccak256 of their concatenation is attestation.publicInputsHash. attestation: what getHistoricalProof(proofHash) returns (subject, proofType, publicInputsHash, expiresAt) and isAttestationRevoked(proofHash) (revoked).

proofHash.description: The Oracle's keccak256(proof, proofType, chainid, oracle). The vectors ship no proof bytes, so it is a stand-in fixture (keccak256 of the verified publicInputsHash, proofType, chainId and oracleAddress words) that a runner never recomputes.

expiresAt.description: Live while the consumer's clock is at or before it.

records.description: What this evaluation writes to the observation store (SPEC.md section 10.8): an insert-if-absent or atomic-maximum write counts even when the store already holds the value, and a record is null only when the evaluation writes nothing of that kind. discovery: the discovery document's updatedAt and its revoked keys (keyId and credentialSigner / signerPubkeyHash), when the discovery steps pass on their own, whatever the evidence, under the attestorProviderId the allowlist pins its trust domain to if the document's entry for the deployment names it, else under null (never shared with another trust domain; a key revocation record is keyed by trust domain, recording attestor or null, keyId and material, so a record under null never stops one under the attestor); revocation: (fetch host, announced evidenceId) from a 410 or a revoked body once steps 1-3 pass; evidence: the active evidence document once steps 1-9 pass (after a conflict the store keeps the first).

heldGrant.description: What this evaluation does to the grant held for its subject, discovery host (trustDomainId) and announced evidenceId (SPEC.md section 10.7, Held grants). A grant past its recorded evidence's expiresAt is ended whatever the outcome, and one past the attestation expiresAt its record carries is ended unless an evaluation of another proof accepts (replaced). When it rests on another proof: replaced (accepted, unless the grant is still exercised at context.now, its recheckBy set and later and its record's attestation expiresAt not passed, and that expiresAt is no earlier than context.proof's: the record now rests on context.proof), ended (refused at step 1, 4, 5, 18, 20 or 29, the evidence's own ends), or untouched (anything else: the grant stays as it was). An accepting evaluation never ends a grant.

unavailable.description: Why the evaluation cannot complete (SPEC.md section 10.5, Block pair): blocks_invalid (the pair fails the validity checks) or blocks_stale (its latest block is older than maxBlockAgeSeconds). seenDiscovery.description: Discovery fixtures in the consumer's observation store, each with the attestorProviderId its key revocations were recorded under: the attestor the consumer pinned its trust domain to on this deployment when it recorded it, if the document's own entry for this deployment named that attestor; null otherwise (they then apply to that trust domain alone, SPEC.md section 10.7, Revocation).

oneOf.description: The ERC-8262 Oracle `providerId` (uint256: nonzero and at most 2^256 - 1) that attests for this trust domain on the paired deployment, as a canonical decimal string. Self-asserted: a consumer accepts it only when it equals the attestor its allowlist pins for the trust domain.

seenEvidence.description: Active evidence fixtures in the consumer's observation store.

seenRevoked.description: (trustDomainId, evidenceId) pairs the consumer recorded as revoked from a 410 or a revoked body, trustDomainId being the allowlisted host it came from.

trustDomainId.description: The independently controlled signing domain: the lowercase DNS host that serves this provider's discovery document and evidence endpoint. A document is authoritative only when fetched over https, without redirects, from this exact host: the consumer compares the serialized host of the URL it fetched with this value as exact ASCII. Never an IP literal: the last label starts with a letter, so no WHATWG URL parser reads the host as an IPv4 address. The host proves nothing about the attestor: the consumer's allowlist pins each trust domain to its attestorProviderId per Oracle deployment, and a host it does not list is refused.

evidenceId.description: Replay: an unguessable capability (at least 128 bits, base64url), unique for the provider's lifetime and never reused. A consumer validates an announced id against this rule before using it, requests exactly `https://{trustDomainId}/v1/erc8262/evidence/` followed by the id, and refuses a body whose evidenceId differs (exact comparison). It keys what it has observed by (trustDomainId, evidenceId). Re-delivery with identical immutable fields is idempotent and counts once; any differing immutable field is refused. Renewal is a new evidenceId.

latest.description: The quorum's latest-block reads (SPEC.md section 10.6), where they differ from the finalized reads the rest of the context gives; null when they are the same. registry and validConfigs as in an evaluation case's latest; each member's isAttestationRevoked reads the same at both blocks.

attestorProviderId.description: The ERC-8262 Oracle `providerId` (uint256: nonzero and at most 2^256 - 1) that attests for this trust domain on the paired deployment, as a canonical decimal string. Self-asserted: a consumer accepts it only when it equals the attestor its allowlist pins for the trust domain.

credentialRoots.description: Roots the Oracle holds valid (isValidCredentialRoot) and registered to the attestor (getCredentialRoot(root).providerId).

blocks.description: The block pair the evaluation (or the quorum) resolved, checked against the consumer's clock (context.now) before its first Oracle read (SPEC.md section 10.5, Block pair; a quorum checks it once every member's fetches have completed, section 10.6): the node's eth_chainId and the finalized and latest blocks' number and timestamp. Invalid when chainId is not the deployment's, the finalized block is after the latest one (number or timestamp; equal is not after), or the latest block's timestamp is more than clockSkewSeconds after the consumer's clock; else stale when the latest block's timestamp is more than maxBlockAgeSeconds before the consumer's clock.

requirement.description: The multi-provider requirement (SPEC.md section 10.6): one claimType, the proof type it must feed, and the statement every member's proof must prove.

claimType.description: The claim, namespaced `<namespace>.<name>`, e.g. `kyc.individual`, `personhood.unique`. Consumers map (sourceId, claimType) to their own scoring policy; a provider never sends points, categories or tiers.

proofType.description: The ERC-8262 proof type the claim feeds: 4 (ATTESTATION, credential-root inclusion), 7 (COMPLIANCE_SIGNED), 8 (RISK_SCORE_SIGNED) or 9 (COMPLIANCE_MULTI_SIGNED).

statement.description: The statement the consumer requires the proof to prove (SPEC.md section 10.5, step 30), tagged with the proof type it is for: null for proof type 4 (the evidence's credentialType is the statement); for 7 the accepted jurisdiction ids and the config_hash; for 8 the risk proof_type and config_hash with, for a threshold (1), its direction (1 GT, 2 LT) and bound_lower, or for a range (2), bound_lower and bound_upper (risk_score_signed leaves the other word free in each mode); for 9 those of 7 plus the least threshold_m.

jurisdictionIds.description: The ERC-8262 jurisdiction ids the consumer accepts.
The ERC-8262 jurisdiction ids the consumer accepts.

status.description: The HTTP status; null when no HTTP response arrived (a timeout, a TLS or connection failure).
The HTTP status; null when no HTTP response arrived (a timeout, a TLS or connection failure).

announcedEvidenceId.description: The evidenceId the consumer was given (announcement or its own record). Not necessarily valid: the consumer checks it against the evidence schema's evidenceId rule before building the URL.

proof.description: The Oracle-verified proof the evidence feeds, as the consumer reads it (SPEC.md section 10.5, steps 30-31). proofHash: the hash the Oracle indexes the proof by, which keys a grant made on it (section 10.7, Held grants). publicInputs: the publicInputs bytes of the submitCompliance call that verified it, as 32-byte lowercase hex words in ERC-8262 order (the section 10.5 layout table); the consumer accepts them only if keccak256 of their concatenation is attestation.publicInputsHash. attestation: what getHistoricalProof(proofHash) returns (subject, proofType, publicInputsHash, expiresAt) and isAttestationRevoked(proofHash) (revoked).

proofHash.description: The Oracle's keccak256(proof, proofType, chainid, oracle). The vectors ship no proof bytes, so it is a stand-in fixture (keccak256 of the verified publicInputsHash, proofType, chainId and oracleAddress words) that a runner never recomputes.

expiresAt.description: Live while the consumer's clock is at or before it.

attestors.description: Distinct attestorProviderIds, in ascending numeric order.

items.description: The ERC-8262 Oracle `providerId` (uint256: nonzero and at most 2^256 - 1) that attests for this trust domain on the paired deployment, as a canonical decimal string. Self-asserted: a consumer accepts it only when it equals the attestor its allowlist pins for the trust domain.

records.description: What each member's evaluation against the snapshot writes, in member order (SPEC.md section 10.6), as an evaluation case's expected.records; null for a member for another claim or proof type, which is not evaluated. On an unusable pair each member still runs the steps that read no block and writes what they write.

oneOf.description: What this evaluation writes to the observation store (SPEC.md section 10.8): an insert-if-absent or atomic-maximum write counts even when the store already holds the value, and a record is null only when the evaluation writes nothing of that kind. discovery: the discovery document's updatedAt and its revoked keys (keyId and credentialSigner / signerPubkeyHash), when the discovery steps pass on their own, whatever the evidence, under the attestorProviderId the allowlist pins its trust domain to if the document's entry for the deployment names it, else under null (never shared with another trust domain; a key revocation record is keyed by trust domain, recording attestor or null, keyId and material, so a record under null never stops one under the attestor); revocation: (fetch host, announced evidenceId) from a 410 or a revoked body once steps 1-3 pass; evidence: the active evidence document once steps 1-9 pass (after a conflict the store keeps the first).
